title: Algebra-target active operators reconstruct interval fibres
statement: Use the ordinary ordered-fibre category $\mathsf{LM}^{\otimes}$ of [def-coef-left-module-operadic-encoding]. For $t\geq0$, put $X_1(t)=(\langle t\rangle,\varnothing)$ and $X_0(t)=(\langle t+1\rangle,\{t+1\})$. For a monotone map $\beta:[q]\to[p]$, where $[t]=\{0,\ldots,t\}$, define the following ordinary arrows, with each displayed fibre ordered increasingly. The arrow $T_\beta:X_1(p)\to X_1(q)$ has fibre $(\beta(i-1),\beta(i)]$ at output $1\leq i\leq q$ and discards every other input. The arrow $K_\beta:X_0(p)\to X_1(q)$ has the same fibres and discards all other inputs, including the module input. The arrow $B_\beta:X_0(p)\to X_0(q)$ has those algebra-output fibres and module-output fibre $(\beta(q),p+1]$, discarding precisely the inputs at most $\beta(0)$. Here $(u,v]$ denotes the list $u+1,\ldots,v$, empty if $u=v$. Write $D^1_\beta=T_\beta$ and $D^0_\beta=K_\beta$. Let $r,s,n\geq0$, let $\alpha:[n]\to[s]$ and $\delta:[n]\to[r]$ be monotone, with $\alpha(0)=0$ and $\alpha(n)=s$, and let $\eta\in\{0,1\}$. Suppose $h:X_\eta(r)\to X_1(s)$ is any arrow of $\mathsf{LM}^{\otimes}$ satisfying $T_\alpha\circ h=D^\eta_\delta$. For $1\leq j\leq s$, let $C_j$ be its ordered fibre at $j$. Define integers $\lambda(0)=\delta(0)$ and $\lambda(j)=\delta(0)+\sum_{l=1}^j|C_l|$ for $1\leq j\leq s$. Then $\lambda$ takes values in $[r]$ and is monotone, $\lambda(s)=\delta(n)$, each $C_j$ is exactly the increasing list $(\lambda(j-1),\lambda(j)]$, and $\lambda\circ\alpha=\delta$. The inputs discarded by $h$ are exactly those at most $\delta(0)$ or greater than $\delta(n)$ (including the module input when $\eta=0$). In particular $h=D^\eta_\lambda$. These conclusions include $s=0$ and empty algebra-output fibres.

source.place: Higher Algebra (2017), Proposition 4.1.2.11, final cartesian-lift calculation; Remark 4.2.2.8, left-module analogue. Agent expansion of the ordered-fibre calculation; no Stacks tag covers this operator-combinatorial assertion. WANTED archive in literature/.

mathlib_searches.query: Interval fibre reconstruction for active Cut operators and cross arrows into algebra words
mathlib_searches.verdict: no match: read all hits. SimplexCategory.Hom.mk and toOrderHom only bundle monotone maps (AlgebraicTopology/SimplexCategory/Defs.lean:77-86); the simplex generators-relations epi-mono factorization concerns an already given simplex arrow. Neither reconstructs ordered LM operator fibres from an equation with an active operator. Profinite words, cuts in ordered fields, ordinary factorization categories and module images have different objects and hypotheses. The targeted grep found no ordered LM operator calculus.
